statutory_clock.scope_reason: Phase 1 significant hazard: risk of harm associated with exposure to damp, mould or fungal growth (regulation 3(2)). In force from 27 October 2025.
statutory_clock.significant_risk_test_encoded: regulation 3(1)(b) as made: a reasonable lessor with the relevant knowledge would take steps to make safe as a matter of urgency (but not within 24 hours). The draft amendment's substitute, 'make safe within 15 working days', is not encoded.

phases_not_in_force.status_on_retrieval: Not made. The legislation.gov.uk page retrieved on 24 October 2026 said this was a draft and had not yet been made as a UK statutory instrument. The draft says it comes into force on 30 November 2026.

deadlines.name: Standard investigation completed
deadlines.note: Ten working days beginning on the day after the day the lessor becomes aware of the issue of concern. Regulation 6 does not apply where regulation 5 Condition 1 applies, so this period is used for a significant hazard and not for an emergency.

deadlines.name: Deadlines that run from investigation completion
deadlines.note: Not calculated. The written summary, significant-hazard safety work, and supplementary preventative work run from the day the investigation is completed. The officer has not recorded that day.

reasonable_endeavours.note: Section 10A(5) is a defence the lessor must prove: that they used all reasonable endeavours to avoid the breach. Regulations 5, 11 and 13 also stop particular duties once all reasonable endeavours to obtain a necessary consent are exhausted. This module does not decide either question.

counting.working_day: Regulation 2: any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday, Christmas Day, Good Friday, or a bank holiday under the Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971 in England and Wales.
counting.day_one: For working-day periods, day 1 is the day after the trigger when that day is a working day, otherwise the next working day. The emergency period is 24 hours and does not skip weekends.
counting.twelve_weeks: A period of 12 weeks beginning with the day after the determination is 84 days beginning with that day, inclusive. The last day is 83 days later.

statutory_hooks.text: In proceedings for breach of the covenant implied by section 10A(2), it is a defence for the lessor to prove that the lessor used all reasonable endeavours to avoid that breach.

Regulations 5(6), 11(3) and 13(5) stop particular duties where work cannot lawfully be done without another person's consent and the lessor has exhausted all reasonable endeavours to obtain it. Recording a step is not a finding that endeavours are exhausted.

reasonable_endeavours.guidance_note: MHCLG guidance retrieved on 24 October 2026 says landlords should keep records of access attempts, correspondence, approvals and attempts to find contractors or accommodation, and that a court decides whether all reasonable endeavours were used. This draft does not decide that.
reasonable_endeavours.note: No visit, call, letter or application has been added by the agent. If the list is empty, that is because the officer has not entered a step. An officer has not approved this record.

landlord_procedure.source: Housing Ombudsman Complaint Handling Code, and the resident pages cited above
landlord_procedure.note: The Code text read on 24 October 2026 did not define 'working day'. This module does not turn those numbers into an operative date. The landlord's own procedure should be checked.

housing_ombudsman.after_the_landlords_final_response: The resident pages read on 24 October 2026 say the Ombudsman can accept a complaint for investigation where the landlord's stage 2 response is dated within 12 months. The agent does not refer the resident and does not decide that the Ombudsman can consider the complaint.
